questions.q: What does "continuous training" (CT) add to a standard CI/CD pipeline?
options: A second copy of the unit test suite
A stage that retrains and re-validates the model on fresh data, triggered independently of any code change
A requirement that every deploy must be manual
Automatic rollback of all database migrations
questions.explain: CT is the ML-specific addition: retraining and re-validating on a schedule or data trigger, separate from code changes.

questions.q: Why is it a problem for a pipeline to only run pytest and ship a container?
options: pytest cannot run in a container
Unit tests check code correctness, not model quality, so a model with degraded accuracy could still pass and deploy
Containers cannot host ML models
pytest requires a GPU to run
questions.explain: Normal test suites verify code behavior, not statistical model quality — a dedicated validation gate is needed to catch accuracy regressions.

questions.q: In the example validate() function, what does checking `auc >= baseline_auc - 0.01` accomplish beyond the minimum AUC check?
options: It guarantees the model trains faster
It blocks a model that is technically above the minimum threshold but still a regression compared to the current production model
It automatically retrains the model if it fails
It is purely decorative and has no functional effect
questions.explain: Comparing against a baseline catches regressions that an absolute threshold alone would miss, since a model could clear the floor and still be worse than what's live.

questions.q: Why does the guide recommend keeping code deploys and model deploys separable in a pipeline?
options: Because Kubernetes forbids deploying both at once
Because it makes it easier to tell, during an incident, which of the two actually changed
Because models cannot be containerized alongside code
Because GitHub Actions only allows one deploy per day
questions.explain: Coupling a code deploy and a model deploy into a single step makes root-causing an incident harder, since you can't isolate which change caused it.

questions.q: In the GitHub Actions example, what is the purpose of the `environment: production` setting on the deploy-production job?
options: It sets the AWS region for the deployment
It allows configuring required reviewers so a human must approve before that job runs, covered further in Lesson 25
It automatically scales the number of replicas
It disables logging for that job
questions.explain: A GitHub environment can be configured with protection rules, including required reviewers, which is how a manual approval gate gets added to an otherwise automated pipeline.
